before.title: Declared averaging kernel, macroscopic scale assumptions and averaged fields
before.statement:
Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following coarse-graining convention for matter. Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its units, its fields and its sources be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the smoothing theorem cited in clause (b).
(a) [Averaging length and kernel] Fix an averaging length $\ell>0$ and a nonnegative function $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ in the Euclidean test-function convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], with $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\eta(x)\,dx=1$; for $\ell>0$ put $\eta_\ell(x):=\ell^{-3}\eta(x/\ell)$ (the scaled family of [[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]] with $n=3$, $\varepsilon=\ell$). The pair $(\ell,\eta)$ is declared data of the model and is held fixed in every statement that uses it.
(b) [Averaged fields] Let $F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$ ($m=1$ or $3$) be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]], read at fixed $t$). Extend $F(\cdot,t)$ by zero outside $\Omega$ and define the averaged field by the convolution integral $$F_\ell(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\eta_\ell(x-y)\,F(y,t)\,dy$$ of [[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]] with kernel $\eta_\ell$ (the real case, read componentwise, of its statement for complex $f$). Then $F_\ell$ is defined on $\mathbb R^3\times I$, and by that lemma, for each fixed $t$, the map $x\mapsto F_\ell(x,t)$ is smooth with $\partial_x^\alpha F_\ell=(\partial^\alpha\eta_\ell)*F$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, derivatives being taken under the integral sign; the lemma also gives the absolute existence and measurability of the convolution and its independence of representatives. On the interior region $\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega)>\ell\}$, the value $F_\ell(x,t)$ is the average of $F(\cdot,t)$ over the ball $B_\ell(x)$ against the weight $\eta_\ell(x-\cdot)$.
(c) [Macroscopic reading and scale separation] The framework reads its macroscopic fields and source densities as such averages only in situations where a separation of microscopic and observation scales is stated for the problem at hand; the averaging length is part of that statement, and no canonical value of $\ell$ is asserted. This is a formulation choice for the macroscopic description, not a consequence of the vacuum equations.
(d) [Boundary handling] On the boundary layer $\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)\le\ell\}$ the average of (b) also averages the zero extension outside $\Omega$. Any other boundary convention (a declared extension of the microscopic field, an imposed boundary-layer model, or restriction of the macroscopic region to the interior of the layer) is an additional model assumption and must be declared where it is used.
(e) [No constitutive content] Coarse graining reorganises the description; it does not by itself produce a constitutive relation between averaged fields and averaged sources, and no linear, local or instantaneous response is asserted by this postulate. Such a response is the separate assumption [[post-em-material-closure]], and the derivation of macroscopic field equations from the vacuum equations is the separate result [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]].
before.strategy: An adopted nonproof formulation. The test-function convention and the local-integrability notion are those of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]; the convolution integral, its scaled family and its smoothness with differentiation under the integral sign are those of [[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]] (kernel $\eta_\ell$, mass one, input $F(\cdot,t)$), a lemma stated under countable choice, which this postulate declares and uses only in the regularity clause (b). The locally integrable class is that of [[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]]. Clause (d) records the boundary extension explicitly rather than silently; clause (e) records that averaging supplies no constitutive law and no field equation. No proof is supplied and none is claimed, in accordance with the nonproof status of a postulate; the source and scope review covers the formulation, its boundary and scale-separation conventions, and its non-derivation.

before.physical_scope: The declared smoothing convention for matter: a fixed smooth unit-mass kernel and averaging length, the definition and interior regularity of the spatial averages of locally integrable fields on the laboratory region, the scale-separation and boundary-layer conventions, and the explicit statement that averaging supplies neither a constitutive law nor a field equation. after.title: Declared averaging kernel, macroscopic scale assumptions and averaged fields
after.statement:
Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following coarse-graining convention for matter. Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its units, its fields and its sources be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the smoothing theorem cited in clause (b).
(a) [Averaging length, kernel and footprint] Fix $\ell>0$ and nonnegative $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\int\eta=1$, in the Euclidean test-function convention of def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions. Put $\eta_\ell(x)=\ell^{-3}\eta(x/\ell)$, $K=\operatorname{supp}\eta$ and choose a declared finite bound $R_\eta>0$ with $K\subseteq\overline B_{R_\eta}(0)$. The kernel and length are fixed data; the imported mass-one mollifier definition does not require $K\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$. At x the exact averaging footprint is $x-\ell K$. Define the open interior averaging domain $$\Omega_{\ell,\eta}:=\{x\in\Omega:x-\ell K\subseteq\Omega\}.$$ The sufficient condition $\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega)>\ell R_\eta$ implies membership. If the additional unit-support condition $K\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$ is declared, the original sufficient region $\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega)>\ell$ and the ball $B_\ell(x)$ are valid special cases; unit support is not inferred from mass one.
(b) [Averaged fields and input regularity] For an open spatial domain V, locally integrable means measurable and absolutely integrable on every compact subset of V, componentwise for maps to $\mathbb R^m$, $m=1$ or 3. First suppose $F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$ has a locally integrable spatial slice $F(\cdot,t)$ for every t under consideration. No integrability across the boundary of Omega is required for the interior branch. Define, for $x\in\Omega_{\ell,\eta}$, $$F_\ell(x,t)=\int_\Omega\eta_\ell(x-y)F(y,t)dy.$$ The compact footprint lies in Omega, so this integral exists absolutely, and for each such t it is smooth in x on $\Omega_{\ell,\eta}$ with $$\partial_x^\alpha F_\ell(x,t)=\int_\Omega(\partial^\alpha\eta_\ell)(x-y)F(y,t)dy$$ for every multi-index. These are applications of the pinned mollifier smoothing supplier after a local compact cutoff, not an assumption that zero extension across the original boundary is locally integrable. For each admissible fixed t the spatial convolution is measurable in x and independent of a.e.-equal spatial representatives; no joint (x,t) measurability follows from the every-slice hypothesis alone. Joint $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ input alone instead gives these slice statements for almost every t, by local Fubini on compact spatial/time exhaustions; it gives no every-time slice claim. A claim for every t must explicitly supply locally integrable slices for every t (for example jointly continuous fields supply that condition). A spacetime a.e. class alone determines the resulting averages only for almost every t; changing an exceptional time slice may change its pointwise-time assignment. Spatial smoothing asserts no time differentiability or joint smoothness without separately stated time hypotheses.
[Compatible extension branch] If a declared extension $\widehat F(\cdot,t)$ agrees with F a.e. on Omega and is locally integrable on an open larger spatial domain V, use the same formula there for all x whose compact footprint lies in V. If $V=\mathbb R^3$ and every declared slice is globally locally integrable, the average is defined and spatially smooth on all $\mathbb R^3\times I$. If only joint local integrability of the extension is supplied, the global spatial conclusion is for almost every t unless the every-slice hypothesis is added. The zero extension is an allowed choice only when it meets this local-integrability condition: equivalently, at each declared t, $\int_{Q\cap\Omega}|F(y,t)|dy<\infty$ for every compact $Q\subset\mathbb R^3$. Mere local integrability inside Omega does not imply that boundary condition. All these extension and per-time conditions are part of the declared configuration, with the original interior branch retaining every locally integrable spatial input.
(c) [Macroscopic reading and scale separation] The framework reads its macroscopic fields and source densities as such averages only in situations where a separation of microscopic and observation scales is stated for the problem at hand; the averaging length and the actual kernel footprint (or its radius bound $\ell R_\eta$) are part of that statement, and no canonical value of $\ell$ is asserted. This is a formulation choice for the macroscopic description, not a consequence of the vacuum equations.
(d) [Boundary handling] For requested averages at $x\in\Omega$, boundary handling concerns the locations where $x-\ell K$ is not contained in the original spatial domain. The region $\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)\le\ell R_\eta\}$ is a sufficient enclosing boundary layer, with $\ell$ in place of $\ell R_\eta$ only in the declared unit-support special case. Every requested average at an exterior location $x\notin\Omega$ must separately satisfy the extension/domain conditions of (b); the interior boundary-layer statement makes no claim to enclose exterior locations. In the interior layer a zero-extension average is used only under the compatible-extension hypothesis of (b). Otherwise one must declare another locally integrable extension, a boundary-layer model with its own well-definedness hypotheses, or restrict the averaging domain to the exact interior footprint domain. No boundary model is supplied by local integrability alone. An extension does not automatically extend a microscopic field equation across the original boundary; any averaging of such equations must either declare their validity on all used extended footprints or retain the resulting boundary distribution terms. These boundary qualifications do not impose a constitutive law.
(e) [No constitutive content] Coarse graining reorganises the description; it does not by itself produce a constitutive relation between averaged fields and averaged sources, and no linear, local or instantaneous response is asserted by this postulate. Such a response is the separate assumption [[post-em-material-closure]], and the derivation of macroscopic field equations from the vacuum equations is the separate result [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]].
after.strategy:
An adopted nonproof formulation: the macroscopic identification and scale-separation/boundary conventions are adopted, not deduced from vacuum Maxwell or asserted empirically. Its mathematical referent is checked against the exact published mollifier contract, which permits any smooth compactly supported mass-one kernel and requires locally integrable input on the region used by its compact translates; it imposes no unit support.

Interior applicability: for x0 in the exact footprint domain, x0-ell K is compact inside Omega. A sufficiently small closed ball of x-values about x0 has all its translated kernel supports in one compact Q contained in Omega. This follows from compactness and openness, and proves the footprint domain open. At each admissible t let f_Q be F(.,t) on Q and zero elsewhere. Since Q is compact inside Omega, f_Q belongs to global L1 and hence L1loc. The published mollifier smoothing theorem applied to f_Q gives a smooth convolution and every derivative by differentiating the kernel. In that small x-neighbourhood it equals the declared interior integral, and every derivative has support inside Q as well. This proves absolute existence, spatial smoothness and the derivative formula for arbitrary interior L1loc data. Spatial a.e. representatives give equal integrals for each x because translated kernel weights are bounded and have compact support. Compactness of K gives its finite support-radius bound; no equality to 1 is assumed.

Slice qualification: exhaust Omega by compact sets K_j={x:|x|<=j,dist(x,R3 minus Omega)>=1/j} (use the usual convention if Omega=R3), and the open laboratory interval by compact subintervals. On each compact product joint local integrability makes F absolutely integrable. Apply the L1 Fubini theorem to these compact restrictions extended by zero to the Euclidean product. Outside a null exceptional time set the spatial integrals on each K_j are finite; a countable union of these exceptional sets is null under the already declared countable-choice convention. Thus a.e. time slices are locally integrable, because every compact subset of Omega lies in some K_j. It does not prove every-time slices or uniquely determine assignments at exceptional times. No time derivative is inferred. The compatible-extension branch uses the same precise supplier with its hypotheses checked on the declared larger domain; the all-space branch applies only when the extension is globally L1loc per slice. Zero extension has that property exactly when its absolute integral on Q equals the finite integral over Q intersect Omega for every global compact Q. A field such as 1/x1 on x1>0 fails this condition, so no unconditional boundary extension is asserted.

The enclosing boundary-layer claim is restricted to x inside Omega; requested exterior averages are governed separately by the footprint/extension conditions. Measurability in the every-slice branch refers to x at each admissible fixed t, with no unassumed joint measurability. Clauses (c)-(e) retain the adopted macroscopic reading, require the actual kernel footprint in scale separation, and distinguish smoothing from constitutive closure and field equations. No deductive proof of this modelling postulate is supplied or claimed. These local applicability arguments and inherited mathematical supplier pins are not independent source/audit acceptance.

before.title: Polarization, magnetization, bound and free sources, and the fields D and H
before.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its units, its fields $E,B$ and its source densities $\rho,J$ be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], and let the averaging convention be that of [[post-em-coarse-graining]], in whose sense the objects below are macroscopic.
(a) [Polarization and magnetization] The material model specifies two maps $P,M:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] on the open set $\Omega\times I$: $P$ is the electric dipole moment per unit volume, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $M$ the magnetic dipole moment per unit volume, in $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, both read in the frame basis. They are data of the chosen material model: this definition does not compute them from $E$ and $B$, and no relation between $(P,M)$ and the fields is asserted here.
(b) [Bound sources] Write $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ for the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] taken at fixed $t$, and $\partial_t$ for the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] at fixed position, and define the bound charge density and bound current density by $$\rho_b:=-\operatorname{div}P,\qquad J_b:=\partial_tP+\operatorname{curl}M.$$ Since $P,M$ are jointly $C^2$, $\rho_b$ and $J_b$ are continuous (indeed $C^1$); $\rho_b$ carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $J_b$ carries $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$.
(c) [Free sources] Define $\rho_f:=\rho-\rho_b$ and $J_f:=J-J_b$, in the same units as $\rho$ and $J$; these are the free charge and free current densities of the model. The decomposition $\rho=\rho_f+\rho_b$, $J=J_f+J_b$ is part of the chosen material model: the same total pair $(\rho,J)$ with a different pair $(P,M)$ is a different model.
(d) [Displacement and magnetic intensity] Define the electric displacement and the magnetic intensity by $$D:=\varepsilon_0E+P,\qquad H:=\mu_0^{-1}B-M,$$ where $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\mu_0,c>0$ are the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; $D$ carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $H$ carries $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-1}$.
(e) [Status] This item fixes objects and the bound/free convention only. No field equation ([[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]]), no constitutive relation ([[post-em-material-closure]]), no conservation of the bound pair ([[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]](a)) and no identification of $P,M$ with microscopic dipole sums is asserted here.
before.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. The regions, fields and sources are those of the named suppliers; the derivatives in (b) are the published divergence, curl and partial derivative; the constants and units are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the $C^2$ class is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the macroscopic reading is the convention of [[post-em-coarse-graining]]. The definition records explicitly that $(P,M)$ are model data read in the laboratory frame basis, that the bound/free split is a modelling choice, and that no constitutive relation between $(P,M)$ and $(E,B)$ is included. Well-definedness of $\rho_b,J_b$ as continuous fields is the componentwise sum/product differentiability calculus of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. No field equation, no derivative of the physical fields and no microscopic interpretation is used.

Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its units, its fields $E,B$ and its source densities $\rho,J$ be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], and let the averaging convention be that of [[post-em-coarse-graining]], in whose sense the objects below are macroscopic. Any convolution used to instantiate that reading is taken on its declared exact interior-footprint domain, or under a declared locally integrable compatible extension covering every used footprint. Its every-time use requires every-time locally integrable spatial slices; joint spacetime local integrability alone supplies only the almost-every-time branch. The joint C2 regularity specified below is a separate model hypothesis, not a consequence of spatial smoothing.
(a) [Polarization and magnetization] The material model specifies two maps $P,M:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] on the open set $\Omega\times I$: $P$ is the electric dipole moment per unit volume, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $M$ the magnetic dipole moment per unit volume, in $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, both read in the frame basis. They are data of the chosen material model: this definition does not compute them from $E$ and $B$, and no relation between $(P,M)$ and the fields is asserted here.
(b) [Bound sources] Write $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ for the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] taken at fixed $t$, and $\partial_t$ for the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] at fixed position, and define the bound charge density and bound current density by $$\rho_b:=-\operatorname{div}P,\qquad J_b:=\partial_tP+\operatorname{curl}M.$$ Since $P,M$ are jointly $C^2$, $\rho_b$ and $J_b$ are continuous (indeed $C^1$); $\rho_b$ carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $J_b$ carries $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$.
(c) [Free sources] Define $\rho_f:=\rho-\rho_b$ and $J_f:=J-J_b$, in the same units as $\rho$ and $J$; these are the free charge and free current densities of the model. The decomposition $\rho=\rho_f+\rho_b$, $J=J_f+J_b$ is part of the chosen material model: the same total pair $(\rho,J)$ with a different pair $(P,M)$ is a different model.
(d) [Displacement and magnetic intensity] Define the electric displacement and the magnetic intensity by $$D:=\varepsilon_0E+P,\qquad H:=\mu_0^{-1}B-M,$$ where $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\mu_0,c>0$ are the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; $D$ carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $H$ carries $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-1}$.
(e) [Status] This item fixes objects and the bound/free convention only. No field equation ([[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]]), no constitutive relation ([[post-em-material-closure]]), no conservation of the bound pair ([[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]](a)) and no identification of $P,M$ with microscopic dipole sums is asserted here.
after.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. The regions, fields and sources are those of the named suppliers; the derivatives in (b) are the published divergence, curl and partial derivative; the constants and units are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the $C^2$ class is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the macroscopic reading is the convention of [[post-em-coarse-graining]], with its actual footprint/compatible-extension and slice hypotheses carried whenever convolution is used. Joint C2 regularity of the model maps is assumed separately; the spatial averaging operation proves neither time differentiability nor the existence of microscopic dipole sums. The definition records explicitly that $(P,M)$ are model data read in the laboratory frame basis, that the bound/free split is a modelling choice, and that no constitutive relation between $(P,M)$ and $(E,B)$ is included. Well-definedness of $\rho_b,J_b$ as continuous fields is the componentwise sum/product differentiability calculus of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. No field equation, no derivative of the physical fields and no microscopic interpretation is used.

counterexamples.zero_extension: Omega={x1>0}, F=1/x1 is locally integrable inside Omega (including all time-independent slices), but its zero extension is not global L1loc near x1=0. Choose an allowed nonnegative smooth unit-mass eta positive near (1/2,0,0), ell=1 and x=(1/2,0,0). On a small boundary-facing cylinder eta(x-y)>=c>0, so integral eta(x-y)/y1 dy diverges like integral_0^delta dy1/y1.
counterexamples.kernel_support: A positive mass-one bump translated to centre3e1 with support in B_(1/4)(3e1) is allowed by the pinned definition. With ell=1, Omega={x1>0}, x=2e1 has dist(x,Omega complement)=2>ell but its footprint lies near -e1 outside Omega; the claimed unit-ball interior formula is not justified.
counterexamples.bad_slice: For an interior plane x1=a1, set g(x)=1/|x1-a1| off that plane and g=0 on it, and F(x,t)=g(x)1_{t=t0}. It is finite-valued measurable. Tonelli integrates its absolute value first in t to zero, since {t0} is null and g is finite; hence F is joint L1loc. At t0, any spatial box meeting that interior plane has integral of g equal to infinity by integral dy1/|y1|, so that slice is not L1loc.
